examples.title: Basic Usage
A Command Palette
Groups, Icons, Descriptions and Hints
examples.code:
<Command
  label="Project"
  placeholder="Search the project"
  actions={[
    {
      id: 'dashboard',
      label: 'Go to dashboard',
      group: 'Navigation',
      icon: <Icon name="house" />,
      hint: (
        <Kbd.Group separator="then">
          <Kbd>G</Kbd>
          <Kbd>D</Kbd>
        </Kbd.Group>
      ),
    },
    {
      id: 'issues',
      label: 'Go to issues',
      group: 'Navigation',
      icon: <Icon name="circle-dot" />,
      hint: (
        <Kbd.Group separator="then">
          <Kbd>G</Kbd>
          <Kbd>I</Kbd>
        </Kbd.Group>
      ),
    },
    {
      id: 'new-issue',
      label: 'New issue',
      group: 'Actions',
      description: 'File a bug or ask for a feature',
      icon: <Icon name="plus" />,
      hint: <Kbd>C</Kbd>,
    },
    {
      id: 'archive',
      label: 'Archive project',
      group: 'Actions',
      description: 'Only an owner can archive a project',
      icon: <Icon name="box-archive" />,
      disabled: true,

    {
      id: 'theme',
      label: 'Dark mode',
      group: 'Settings',
      icon: <Icon name="moon" />,
      hint: <Tag color="info">New</Tag>,

/>

examples.title: How It Matches
examples.code:
<Command
  label="Settings"
  placeholder="Try “theme” or “mail”"
  empty="No settings match"
  actions={[
    { id: 'dark', label: 'Dark mode', keywords: ['theme', 'appearance'] },
    { id: 'font', label: 'Font size', keywords: ['text', 'zoom'] },
    {
      id: 'notifications',
      label: 'Notifications',
      description: 'Email and push alerts',
      keywords: ['mail'],
    },
    { id: 'language', label: 'Language', description: 'English' },
  ]}
/>

accessibility:
- **The roles:** the field is `role="combobox"` with `aria-autocomplete="list"` and
  `aria-haspopup="listbox"`, and the list is a `listbox` of `option`s, the ARIA 1.2 combobox the
  ARIA Authoring Practices describe. A group is a `group` named by its heading.
- **Focus stays in the field:** the highlighted item is the field's `aria-activedescendant`, and
  the only item that's `aria-selected`. When a key moves it, it's scrolled into view. A click on an
  item keeps focus in the field too.
- **`aria-expanded`** is `true` while the list has an item in it, with `aria-controls` pointing
  at it, and `false` while only the empty message shows.
- **Names:** `label` names the field and the list, and in `Command.Dialog` the dialog as well.
  It's "Commands" unless you give one. An `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` on `Command.Input`,
  `Command.List` or `Command.Dialog` names that one instead.
- **An item is named by its label alone,** and described by its description and hint, so a
  screen reader says what it does first and the rest after. Its icon is hidden.
- **Disabled items** are `aria-disabled`, reachable with the arrows, never run, and never
  highlighted when the list changes.
- **The empty message** is announced through a polite status region when your typing brings it on
  screen, once each time the matches run out, and after `isLoading` ends. An empty search
  announces nothing.
- **No count is announced,** as with [`Combobox`](https://bestax.io/docs/api/form/combobox#a-result-count): a screen
  reader reads how many items there are from the list itself, and a count read out on each
  keystroke talks over the typing.
- **The dialog** is a modal `dialog` with `aria-modal`, around the Command's box, inside a
  `Modal` that's `role="presentation"`. Focus moves to the search field when it opens, stays
  inside while it's open, and goes back to where it was when it closes. The page behind it
  doesn't scroll.
- **The shortcut** never fires while someone is typing, so it can't swallow a letter, and it
  leaves a key the page has already used alone. Nothing announces it, so put it on a button with
  `aria-keyshortcuts`, and show it with `Kbd`.
- **Forced colors:** in Windows high contrast mode the highlight is drawn as an outline in the
  system's highlight color, and a disabled item takes the system's color for disabled text.
- **No motion:** nothing animates.
summary: The `Command` component is a search field over a list of things to do, which narrows as you type and runs the top match on Enter: inline by default, and a command palette in a modal as `Command.Dialog`. Given `actions`, it's one element. It renders the field, the list, the groups and the empty message, and filters the actions by label, keywords and description as the user types, with label matches first. `filter` takes over the matching, for fuzzy search. Built from parts, the app owns the items: what's in the list and how it's filtered, from the search `onQueryChange` reports. Nothing filters them, so a server's answer shows as it came. Either way, focus stays in the field, and the highlighted item is its `aria-activedescendant`. The first enabled item is highlighted whenever the items change, so Enter runs the top match. Running an item calls its own `onSelect`, then the Command's. When typing leaves the empty message on screen, its text is announced through a polite status region, once, after any loading ends. Result counts aren't announced: a screen reader reads the list's size from the markup, and a count on every keystroke talks over the typing.

props.name: actions
props.description: The actions, for a Command that renders the field, the list, the groups and the empty message itself. Typing filters them by label, keywords and description, ignoring case, with label matches first. Leave it out to build the Command from parts.

props.name: filter
props.description: Takes over the filtering, with `actions`: it's handed the search as typed and every action, and returns the ones to show, in the order to show them, which is how to plug in fuzzy matching or cut the list short. It's called with an empty search too.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: The field's placeholder, with `actions`.

props.name: empty
props.description: What shows in place of the list, with `actions`, when nothing matches. It's announced the way `Command.Empty` is. `null` shows nothing.

props.name: children
props.description: The parts, in order: `Command.Input`, then `Command.List` while there are items and `Command.Empty` while there aren't. Nothing filters them, so render the items that match the search `onQueryChange` reports. With `actions` there are none to give: children given with it are ignored, with a warning in development.

props.name: label
props.description: What the Command is for, such as "Commands" or "Settings". It's never shown: it names the search field and the list for assistive tech, and in `Command.Dialog` the dialog too. An empty string counts as none.

props.name: query
props.description: The search, controlled: the text in the field. Pair it with `onQueryChange`.

props.name: defaultQuery
props.description: The search to start with when uncontrolled.

props.name: onQueryChange
props.description: Called with the search as the user types it. Built from parts, this is where the app filters its items.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Called with the picked item's `value`, an action's `id`, when it's run with Enter or a click, after the item's own `onSelect`. A disabled item is never run.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes.

extraProps.name: ref
extraProps.description: Ref forwarded to the `div.command` around the field and the list.

parts.summary: The search field, with the combobox role and the keys, rendered as an `Input` with a search icon.

props.name: iconLeft
props.description: Icon props for left icon. Bulma gives control icons `pointer-events: none`, so a clickable node here never receives a click. Put a button beside the input in its own addon `Control` instead.

props.name: iconRight
props.description: Icon props for right icon. Bulma gives control icons `pointer-events: none`, so a clickable node here never receives a click. Put a button beside the input in its own addon `Control` instead.

props.name: iconLeftName
props.description: Shortcut for left icon name.

props.name: iconRightName
props.description: Shortcut for right icon name.

props.name: iconLeftSize
props.description: Shortcut for left icon size.

props.name: iconRightSize
props.description: Shortcut for right icon size.

props.name: hasIconsLeft
props.description: Force left icon container.

props.name: hasIconsRight
props.description: Force right icon container.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Shows a loading spinner on the `Control` it renders. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the spinner stops and stays drawn (with bestax's CSS loaded). The spinner sits at the right edge, where `iconRight` also sits, and the two overlap; leave the right icon out while loading.

props.name: isExpanded
props.description: Expand the control.

props.name: controlSize
props.description: Control size.

props.name: controlClassName
props.description: Additional CSS classes for the Control.

props.name: color
props.description: Bulma color modifier for the input.

props.name: size
props.description: Size modifier for the input.

props.name: isRounded
props.description: Rounded input corners.

props.name: isStatic
props.description: Styles the input as static text. It stays editable; add `readOnly` to stop edits.

props.name: isHovered
props.description: Applies hovered state.

props.name: isFocused
props.description: Applies focused state.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes to apply.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disabled input.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Read-only input.

parts.summary: Items under a heading, a `group` named by it.

props.name: label
props.description: The heading, which also names the group for assistive tech, unless you give the group an `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` of its own.

props.name: children

parts.summary: One thing to do in the list, named by its label and described by its description and hint.

props.name: value
props.description: What the Command's `onSelect` hands back. Unique within the Command.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Can't be run. The arrows still reach it, so a screen reader user finds it, and it's never `aria-selected`.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Runs the item, when it's picked with Enter or a click, before the Command's `onSelect`.

props.name: icon
props.description: Shown before the label, and hidden from assistive tech.

props.name: description
props.description: A line under the label. A screen reader hears it after the label, as the item's description.

props.name: hint
props.description: Shown at the end of the row, such as a keyboard shortcut in a `Kbd.Group`, or a `Tag`. It only shows. A screen reader hears it after the label, with the description.

props.name: children
props.description: The label, which names the item.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes.

parts.summary: The message shown in place of the list when nothing matches, announced when typing brings it on screen.

props.name: children
props.description: The message, such as "No commands match". Its text is announced when typing brings it on screen and isn't read again while it stays, so a message that names the search is heard for the first search only.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes.

parts.summary: The Command in a modal, a command palette, opened by its `shortcut` or by `open`, that closes once an item has run. It renders nothing while it's closed. Open, it's a `Modal` with a background and the Command's box as the `dialog`, named by `label`: focus goes to the search field, Tab stays inside, Escape and a click on the background close it, the page behind it doesn't scroll, and focus goes back to where it was when it closes.

props.name: actions
props.description: The actions, for a Command that renders the field, the list, the groups and the empty message itself. Typing filters them by label, keywords and description, ignoring case, with label matches first. Leave it out to build the Command from parts.

props.name: filter
props.description: Takes over the filtering, with `actions`: it's handed the search as typed and every action, and returns the ones to show, in the order to show them, which is how to plug in fuzzy matching or cut the list short. It's called with an empty search too.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: The field's placeholder, with `actions`.

props.name: empty
props.description: What shows in place of the list, with `actions`, when nothing matches. It's announced the way `Command.Empty` is. `null` shows nothing.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled open state. When set, opening and closing only report through `onOpenChange`.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Initial open state when uncontrolled.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called with the open state asked for: `true` from the `shortcut`, and `false` from Escape, a click on the background, or a pick while `closeOnSelect` is on. Fires in controlled and uncontrolled use.

props.name: shortcut
props.description: A key combination that opens the dialog from anywhere on the page, such as `"mod+k"`: modifiers and a key joined by `+`, where `mod` is Ctrl or ⌘ (either one, on every platform), and the others are `ctrl`, `meta`, `alt` and `shift`. It's ignored while the user is typing in a text field, a select or editable content, while an IME is composing, while a modal overlay is open (a `Modal`, a `Dialog`, a `Sidebar` with its overlay or a full-page `Loading`), and when something else has already used the key. It only opens the dialog. Off unless given.

props.name: closeOnSelect
props.description: Closes the dialog once an item has run. Turn it off for an item that opens another page of the palette, and close it yourself with `open`.

props.name: clearOnClose
props.description: Clears the search when the dialog closes: an uncontrolled one itself, and a controlled one through `onQueryChange('')`.

props.name: portal
props.description: Renders the dialog into a portal target instead of inline. Forwarded to the underlying `Modal`; see its `portal` prop for the accepted values.

props.name: children
props.description: The parts, in order: `Command.Input`, then `Command.List` while there are items and `Command.Empty` while there aren't. Nothing filters them, so render the items that match the search `onQueryChange` reports. With `actions` there are none to give: children given with it are ignored, with a warning in development.

props.description: The search to start with when uncontrolled.

props.description: Called with the search as the user types it. Built from parts, this is where the app filters its items.
